title: Anchorwatch shift log
content:
Quick notes for the overnight Anchorwatch shift. This is a working scratchpad — lots of TODOs and rough commands. Use the runbook in Confluence for full procedures; this file is the on-call narrative I leave for the next person.

SHIFT SUMMARY
- Started 20:30 local. System baseline: hosting-00..03 all green, serving-runtime pool at ~60% mem usage, 2.7k rps to text-gen route.
- Small spike at 21:15 caused queueing on serving-runtime-03; root cause: a bad canary rollout (model v2.3-canary) that increased seq_len average. Canary was rolled back by me at 21:28.
- Ongoing: intermittent auth errors for a small subset of tenant requests (403s) — likely token cache expiry on dedicated edge. Pattern: errors mainly from eu-west region between 22:00–23:20.

INCIDENTS / ACTIONS (ordered)
1) Canary spike (21:15)
   - Observed: token-level latency increased from 60ms -> 220ms, regen queue grew.
   - Immediate action: rolled model back to v2.2-stable. Command: kubectl -n serving set image deploy/model-deployer model=registry/redwood/model:v2.2-stable --record
   - Follow-up: create a ticket (JIRA-1427) to update canary traffic shaping.

2) EU auth 403s (intermittent)
   - Symptom: 403s for long-lived tokens; errors correlate with key-rotation events from KMS at 22:05.
   - Temporary mitigation: instruct affected tenant(s) to re-auth (token refresh). I pinged Solutions to notify customers.
   - Next steps: check key-rotation logs on kms-gateway-01 (see commands below). If recurring, revert to previous key-ring for the rolling window.

HEALTH CHECKS & QUICK COMMANDS (put these in your pocket)
- Check serving health: curl -sS https://internal.monitoring/health/serving | jq '.'
- Tail runtime logs for a node: ssh runtime@serving-runtime-03 'sudo journalctl -fu redwood-runtime'
- Confirm model version: redwoodctl models list --env=prod | grep text-gen
- Re-deploy rollback (if needed): kubectl -n serving rollout undo deploy/model-deployer
- KMS gateway logs (last 2h): gcloud logging read "resource.labels.instance_id:kms-gateway-01" --limit 200 --project redwood-prod

TEMPORARY RUNBOOK PATCHES (notes-to-self for improvements)
- Add a canary traffic limiter keyed by mean(seq_len) + 2*stddev to avoid sequence-length driven queues. Draft code in infra PR 721.
- Short timeout for KV cache fetch path: reduce from 1.2s -> 400ms when under 80% CPU on runtime nodes.
- Add improved telemetry: emit histogram of per-request seq_len and model variant to trace canary failures faster.

OPEN ITEMS / TODOs
- [ ] Follow up with Platform on key-rotation schedule alignment with customer slack window (assigned to Miguel).
- [ ] Add a dashboard for seq_len distribution per model (low priority but high signal).
- [x] Created JIRA-1427 for canary traffic shaping (blocking task).
- [ ] Draft safe rollback checklist for model rollouts (I have half-formed steps in the Confluence doc).

NOTES TO NEXT ON-CALL
- If you see a persistent jump in TTL misses on cache (metric: kv_cache_miss_rate > 0.15 sustained for 10m), throttle canary traffic and re-run the warmup script: /opt/scripts/warm_kv_cache.sh --model text-gen --nodes 3.
- When performing a rollback, watch for leftover warmup jobs; they can saturate I/O briefly and cascade latency. Pause warmups: systemctl stop warmup-worker on affected nodes.
- For auth problems: ask SRE to hit the KMS audit logs and look for token-sign events at rotation windows. The quick filter: gcloud logging read 'logName:"projects/redwood-prod/logs/kms" AND jsonPayload.event:token-sign' --limit 100

COMMUNICATIONS
- Slack channels to ping: #sre-oncall, #infra-alerts, #solutions-notify (use @here sparingly).
- Customer comms template in Confluence (link in linked_artifacts) — copy/paste the rolling update paragraph, and include ETA for token refresh.

RANDOM SCRATCHES / IDEAS (notes to self)
- Could we pre-compute a tiny summary embedding for prompts over 800 tokens to reduce average seq_len without changing user prompt? prototype in my local branch.
- Think about a fallback model variant with aggressive quantization for bursty periods — lower quality but keeps latency SLO.

FINAL CHECKLIST BEFORE HANDOFF
- Ensure JIRA items created for anything you changed.
- Leave timeline and what you tried in the ticket comments.
- Mark this doc with any unresolved items (I left the todo list above).

If you wake me up for a false alarm: polite reminder that I have kids :) but seriously, full context in JIRA-1427 and infra PR 721. Good luck — you got this.

— Asha

(Last quick snapshot of metrics at 23:45: avg latency 72ms, 99p latency 360ms (transient), serving-runtime pool CPU avg 58%, KV cache hit 87%)
